channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Chris Godwin caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
item.description: The only positive to take from this is every Tampa Bay receiver who caught a pass clobbered their production from the week before. Godwin did have a 12-yard rush, but it’s another clunker for the wideout in a year where Godwin has yet to reach 50 yards. It’s a mistake to bet that mark will be reached in Week 11 against the Lions after their bye.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Cade Otton caught 4-of-6 targets for 25 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
item.description: Otton was targeted a couple of times in the end zone, but Baker Mayfield wasn’t able to connect with the tight end on either attempt. The 25 yards are his most since Week 5, but it’s still a middling — at best — effort for the 27-year-old. Fantasy managers should look elsewhere in Week 11 against the Lions after Tampa Bay’s bye.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Emeka Egbuka caught 3-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
item.description: It was Egbuka’s first game since Week 6 because of his foot injury, and it was pretty similar to his previous efforts in 2026. He was able to get lose for a 21-yard catch from the arm of Baker Mayfield, but once again, he was unable to eclipse 50 yards; a mark he hasn’t bested since Week 3. Egbuka is a high-floor, low-ceiling WR3 going forward, and the next chance will come after a bye in Week 11 against the Lions.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Tez Johnson caught 2-of-5 targets for 76 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears.
item.description: Johnson’s 58-yard connection with Baker Mayfield set up a rushing score from Bucky Irving. He also had two big drops on third down that would have kept drives going for the Bucs, and on the first he was seen taking out his frustration on his helmet. Johnson ended up leading the Bucs in receiving yards and tied for the lead in targets, but that’s not quite the compliment it should be. Johnson and Tampa Bay get a bye before a showdown with the Lions in Week 11.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Kalif Raymond caught 4-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
item.description: Raymond had a quiet day, but made a huge 13-yard catch on the final drive that ended with a Cairo Santos’ game-winning field goal. Luther Burden exited the game with a head injury late, and if Burden can’t go in Week 11 after the bye, Raymond will be an intriguing dart throw for that contest. If Burden can go, he’s tough to trust in redraft formats.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Colston Loveland caught 4-of-6 targets for 54 yards in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
item.description: Loveland’s fantasy day was salvaged on a 38-yard pass on the final drive of the game where the Buccaneers chose to just forget about the tight end on the busted coverage of busted coverages. Outside of that connection, it was a tough night for the second-year receiver. Loveland will look to do a little earlier damage after the bye in Week 10 against the Lions.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-7 targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
item.description: Odunze couldn’t quite haul in a touchdown throw from Caleb Williams on the first drive of the game, but on the next play, he was able to reach the end zone for his first touchdown of the 2026 season. He could have had another, but a perfect throw from Williams bounced off his hands with nothing but green grass in front of him. Still, it’s another competent game for the former first-round pick, and he’s reached 60 yards in each of his last three contests. Odunze belongs in the WR3 range for Week 11 against the Saints after a Week 10 bye.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: D’Andre Swift rushed 12 times for 31 yards in the Bears’ Week 9 win over the Buccaneers.
item.description: Swift didn’t catch his lone target in a bust of a contest for the veteran tailback. He had a long gain of just six yards, and was nearly outrun by Salvon Ahmed who finished with 25 yards on the ground. Yes, that Salvon Ahmed. It’s a disappointing — but not terribly surprising — follow-up to the three touchdowns he had Monday night in Week 8, but this is what Swift has done throughout his career. He’ll be a RB2 for Week 11 against the Saints after the Bears’ enjoy their bye.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Kenny Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 9 loss to the Bears, adding three catches for 60 yards.
item.description: Most of Gainwell’s yardage came on a 44-yard busted coverage that set up the Bucs’ first score of the game. He found little room in the run game after gashing the Falcons for 140 yards. The 1A/1B talk that head coach Todd Bowles mentioned with Gainwell and Bucky Irving never really came to fruition, as Irving was much more effective with 97 yards on the ground and a pair of scores. Gainwell remains a RB3 going forward, with his next chance to contribute coming in Week 11 against the Lions after their bye.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Luther Burden left Week 9’s game against the Buccaneers with an apparent injury. He finished with 7 catches for 97 yards and a touchdown before exiting.
item.description: Burden fumbled and set up Tampa Bay’s tying score in the fourth quarter after a shot that could have easily been a helmet-to-helmet penalty. The 22-year-old did most of his damage on a 58-yard score that gave Chicago a 14-0 lead. Burden will assuredly undergo concussion testing, but it’s worth noting the Bears don’t play again until Week 11 against the Lions because of a bye.- Christopher Crawford
